Furthermore, this study investigates the impact of iron's ferromagnetic arrangements on the energy and spin landscape within each field effect transistor. It is determined that the charge controlling gates can control the flow of spin polarized electrons through the use of electric fields, while the influence of magnetic gates on spin polarized electrons is similar to that of electric fields applied to the charge flow. As a result, it is possible to independently control the flow of up and down spin polarized electrons, indicating the feasibility of using magnetic gates to control the flow of spin polarized electrons, in addition to the more conventional electric fields.

Cargo, a package manager for the Rust language, boasts a substantial library collection on its platform, Cargo registry. To identify crates susceptible to supply chain attacks, we conducted a study to determine which packages must be updated to resolve security vulnerabilities. By developing the UpdateR tool, we automated the update process and integrated our method with existing security screening processes. Our analysis covered the top 200 Cargo libraries by dependency count and their dependencies, focusing on whether their updated versions would affect updating Cargo itself. The results showed that 42.5% of Cargo's latest crate versions still contain vulnerabilities, with up to 72% of their dependencies affected. Specifically, 17% of the top 200 crates have dependencies that would not be analyzed by traditional security screening tools, highlighting the importance of our method.

This study examines the ergodic behavior of stochastic complex equations on a confined domain with jump processes affecting both the equations and their linear parts. These processes model the impact of pure jump noise in nonlinear stochastic systems, such as a version of the stochastic Landau-Lifshitz equation. Firstly, it establishes average dissipation bounds for solutions of these equations. Secondly, it proves the existence of a Feller transition semigroup, implying that jump noise enables ergodicity in these stochastic equations. Additionally, it explores how transition measures converge as time goes to infinity and investigates the relationship between transition operators, especially in the context of large deviation theory for nonlinear systems.
We provide a detailed analysis and examples for the minimum degree in the power graph for certain non-cyclic abelian groups, ensuring a comprehensive proof is included.

Despite a highly increased energy of the Large Hadron Collider in the billions of electron volts, researchers have successfully re-created and studied particle interactions occurring at the CERN's Intersecting Storage Rings, which involved lower-energy particle collisions in the ten millions of electron volts range. 

The creation of the J/psi particle from the binding of a charm-anticharm quark and another charm-anticharm quark was possible through two distinct methods. One method involved the direct creation of the four quark system from the colliding protons. The alternative method involved an intermediate state of three quarks (c $\bar{c}$$\gamma$) by emitting a virtual photon from the system of two quarks. 

To determine which of these two methods dominates particle interaction, researchers compared the frequency of J/psi creation in full collisions to those resulting from the three quark intermediate process. 

This comparison can be broken down into two factors. Firstly, the frequency with which particles release energy in the form of a virtual photon, which was measured at lower energies of the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider and other experiments. The second factor is the 'form factor' of the large particle, which describes how well it can emit virtual photons. 

Since the J/psi particle is relatively small and tightly bound, it might not efficiently release these high amounts of energy, making the 'form factor' relatively weak and making this process extremely rare.

This research introduces Landmark Gabor Filters (LGFs), which integrate Gabor filters at crucial image feature points to create more resilient and refined image representations. By incorporating a small number of gabor-filtered landmarks, LGFs boost the performance of subsequent tasks, such as patch-based orientation estimation, by enhancing robustness to misalignments and improving discriminative power. Notably, LGFs achieve comparable or superior results to using all image gabor filters with only a fraction of the computational cost. Furthermore, a novel algorithm for optimally selecting these landmark filters for optimized performance is investigated.

Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have achieved significant success in solving various graph-related tasks. However, GCNs typically require sequential processing from message passing to aggregated feature combination, which results in numerous data dependencies and inefficient computation utilization. The introduction of self-attention mechanisms in attention-based GCNs has enabled parallel processing within the layer, but data dependencies persist across layers. To address this, the proposed Graph Reorder Network (GRN) introduces a reorder operation at the end of each GCN layer to independently process features for the subsequent layer. By optimizing data fetching order, GRN reduces computational stalls on accelerated GCNs. Additionally, incorporating learnable network components, the GRN can adaptively configure complex computation flows for diverse graph datasets. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms existing baseline models.

Neural network model extraction, also referred to as functional modeling, has gained significant attention in the field of safety-critical systems due to its capacity to protect embedded networks from malicious attacks. Previous research in this area has predominantly relied on supervised model extraction through Trojan attacks, training a polynomial regression model using training data obtained from target neural networks. Our proposed method deviates from this approach, exploiting the transition functions of quantized neural networks to derive semi-structured samples with minimal additional queries. By incorporating a space partitioning strategy, our model extraction framework can efficiently extract full-precision, structured feed-forward neural networks in a low-dimensional space. The effectiveness of our technique is validated via multiple case studies, demonstrating its ability to extract a quantized DLA network with just 0.07% semi-structured samples. The proposed method further enhances its effectiveness by using a small number of image transformations to obtain low-dimension semi-structured samples. Notably, the proposed space partitioning strategy incorporates an optimality principle, outperforming baseline approaches in Model Extraction. The benefits of our approach model can be twofold: assisting researchers in understanding neural network behavior or enabling an attacker to utilize an accurate proxy model for various malicious purposes.

ROSIE IFU, a groundbreaking instrument, will be integrated into the Submillimeter Telescope in 2023 and allows for detailed 3D chemical analysis of celestial objects. By providing three-dimensional spectra, it will make it possible to examine nebulae, galaxies, and other astronomical formations at a much higher resolution and detail. Although its science cases primarily focus on mapping spatial two-dimensional structures, we propose a unique technique to reconstruct 3D objects using its data and extend our method to apply to specific scenarios such as nebulae, spiral galaxies, and voids. By analyzing line-of-sight velocity variations in its spectra, we demonstrate the capability to determine the depth of each voxel, thereby creating more accurate 3D models. Additionally, we discuss the benefits and potential pitfalls of our approach, highlighting the need to carefully interpret reconstructed images and the need to develop alternative methods for object validation. Overall, our proposed method offers an innovative approach for mapping complex astronomical structures and can be applied to a wide range of objects and scenarios.

A comprehensive theoretical understanding of low-energy astrophysical S-factors, which govern nuclear fusion reactions in stars, is presented. These are examined within a general framework applicable to any such reaction. Using the relativistic Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov framework, which minimizes the relativistic variational action, scientists can achieve a fundamental description of basic nuclear properties such as binding energy, size, and density distribution. This theoretical approach enables researchers to achieve comparable results to non-relativistic models by maintaining consistency with experimental data through a few fundamental relativistic interaction constants, thereby eliminating the need for empirical adjustments.

Researchers find that a significant number of Earth-sized planets orbiting within the habitable zones of Sun-like stars are located beyond the zones where water exists in liquid form. It's unlikely these planets have identical geological structures and internal compositions to Earth. Nevertheless, these stars are valuable for searching for signs of life because they are more likely to be free from certain complex chemical patterns, or 'complexity', in their mineral composition. This could increase the likelihood of detecting complex life forms through the study of their atmospheric biosignatures. It's also possible that the absence of complex life or its complex nature might be indicated by complex patterns of geochemical 'bioshields' - a global chemical cycle linking geological processes and biological activity.

This research focuses on addressing the problem of single stream massive MIMO in an asymmetric QAM system. By applying attention-based channel state information, we can select relevant frequency subbands and enhance feature learning ability. This allows the model to channel-aware select the most meaningful features in complex MIMO systems. Consequently, this improves the performance of message passing based single stream massive MIMO channel coding. Experimental results show that with attention mechanism, we can achieve near capacity performance while reducing massive MIMO system complexity by delivering asymmetrical performance subband selection.

This investigation utilizes a topological setting to examine modern logic's semantic approaches. By leveraging the flexibility of bicategorical methods, we can integrate various semantics types, including those for spatial temporal logic, reasoning about concurrency, and higher-order logic. Our analysis demonstrates that bicategorical constructions are sufficient to reconstruct key aspects of modern logic's diverse semantics and reveals the underlying similarities between them. By doing so, our framework highlights the fundamental similarities between these seemingly distinct approaches to semantic analysis.

The $\mathsf{se}$-index of a graph $G$, denoted as $\mathsf{se}(G)$, is the least number of colors needed to strongly color the edges of $G$. A $\mathsf{se}$-index coloring is effective when every edge-connected subgraph with more than one edge uses different colors. Initially, in 1990, the Weichsel conjecture proposed that the $\mathsf{se}$-index of any bipartite graph with a maximum degree of 3 is 5 or less. In this research, it is shown that the bipartite graphs, which are 5-regular and contain a path of length 5, can exist. Consequently, the Weichsel conjecture was confirmed for any bipartite graph with a maximum degree of 3.

The minimal size of support required for functions within specific eigenspaces of Hamming graphs has been investigated, particularly for cases where the degree of the graph, denoted as i, exceeds half the total variables n. Utilizing the duality between eigenspaces and codes, this study addresses that question under the condition that i exceeds n divided by two by introducing the concept of a new parameter, the minimal support size, for eigensphere functions of support length n minus 2i. When it comes to orthogonal polynomials, specifically Kravcheck's, the study establishes that this new parameter is equal to the minimum support required for functions within specific eigenspaces under four distinct scenarios, each varying based on the values of n and i, with support sizes either 2i or 2i plus one, and supports based on the q base for non-orthogonal polynomials, giving a general increase in the minimal support size compared to q being one, where the size increase is supported by an explicit construction using a Legendre function.

This paper introduces ShinyRPathShinyCOPASI, an R/Shiny package that integrates COPASI models, allowing for various features not available in the standalone version of COPASI. Firstly, users can load and develop models via the COPASI API, providing flexibility in model management. Secondly, scenarios can be created, facilitating comparison of model simulations. Thirdly, sensitivities can be computed through the API, offering insights into model behavior.Lastly, optimization problems can be established and solved within ShinyCOPASI, enabling parameter adjustment to achieve desired objectives. Additionally, users can interact with COPASI models through a user-friendly web interface, gaining real-time feedback and the ability to adjust settings as needed. Furthermore, users can export their optimized models to popular external tools, providing more options in advanced modeling.

Deep neural networks have emerged as a versatile tool for addressing intricate inverse problems, characterized by extensive data. This advantage also translates to problems suited for statistical estimation, enabling the construction of a versatile solver through a pre-built database. Consequently, neural solutions offer an efficient alternative to computationally intensive iterative methods, particularly for issues arising from noisy data or excessive constraints. This work delves into solving such problems using neural methods. It specifically examines issues in是非 problem solving, tomographic image reconstruction from limited views, direct image conversion, inverse problems in the Fourier domain, and non-linear problems with global models. It also delves into various loss functions that can be employed to address these intricate problems.

We investigate the algebra $\mathcal{Z}(C^*(\mathbb{G}))$ of classical functions on a quantum group $\mathbb{G}$ whose reduced C*-algebra is the group C*-algebra of a nonabelian free group, specifically examining the properties of this algebra for pseudocoxeter and certain other quantum groups. Our analysis shows that for $SU_q(2)$, this algebra forms a maximal minimal self-adjoint algebra, while for the quantum permutation group, it also exhibits this property and contains rich subalgebras with interesting characteristics.

In this study, we investigate the feasibility of applying inexact GMRES to find precise policy differences as an inexact method for fixed-policy analysis, in contrast to the traditional approach of precisely evaluating each policy. By doing so, we can reduce the computational load and accelerate convergence in large-scale Markov decision processes. Through the incorporation of inexact calculations, we can perform each policy update as quickly as possible while maintaining precise enough values to guarantee the new policy will outperform its predecessor. As a result, we can compare the performance of traditional policy iteration and the proposed inexact GMRES policy iteration, which can converge within a certain number of iterations, rather than value-error-reducing iterations. Specifically, in our numerical experiments, inexact GMRES policy iteration required only 1000 epochs to reach a precise solution for a 10000-state problem, and was 1000 times faster than traditional policy iteration, which typically takes 10000 value errors to halve its difficulty. Additionally, the proposed method has been successfully applied in the solution of optimal policies for complex reinforcement learning problems, including Gridworld and Mini Chess. Notably, the method has even been used to learn optimal policies in high-dimensional continuous control problems, such as HalfCheetah, AntDrive, and AntWalk, using a neural network approximation for the policy difference function.

We establish a relationship between the symbolic powers and edge ideals of oriented graphs with non-negative weights. Specifically, for any given s, t in the set of positive integers, the symbolic power of the edge ideal I_s(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G}) can expressed as I^{I_s(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G})} for specific degree. Here, I(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G}) represents the edge ideal of an oriented graph with non-negative weights and I^{I_s(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G})} denotes the integer part of the symbolic quotient I^{(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G})}_s\ I I^{-\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G})}_s by I of I^{(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G})}_s. Furthermore, if a specific condition is satisfied, we derive an exact expression for the symbolic power I^{(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G})}_s for any given positive integer s, and we identify a necessary and sufficient condition for the equality I^{(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G})}_{m\ell} = I^{\ell} I^{(\mathbb{S}, \mathbb{G})}_m for the symbolic powers of graph ideals in characteristic zero.

Optimizing a computer simulator is a crucial prerequisite for solving intricate inverse problems. Currently, this optimization process is carried out manually by users who are often specialists in a particular field, such as doctors or geologists. However, their individual preferences in tuning may not necessarily improve the overall usability of the simulator for a wider community. A more collaborative and systematic approach is required to enhance the inverse problem solutions within any given field. In this study, a novel method utilizing adjoint simulations to evaluate the impact of tuning choices on inverse solutions is introduced. By applying this approach, essential parameters can be tuned efficiently to achieve better optimization results. The utility of this approach is demonstrated through a practical example of electromagnetic data modeling and parameter estimation.

This research delves into distribution-free robust learning within the constraints of concept learning and lossless compression, taking into account the role of a defined query radius 'r'. It is established that distribution-free robust learning within a radius of 'r < 1/3' is theoretically equivalent to distribution-specific robust learning with a radius of 'r + ε', where 'ε' represents an infinitesimally small value, and this relationship is both query-class and loss-function dependent. Furthermore, a novel method is introduced to transform any lossless coding scheme into a corresponding robust decoder, enabling distribution-free robust learning for the intersection of class 'C' and the concept sphere with radius '1/3'. Notably, this scheme is shown to yield optimal decoders when applied to the class of symmetric concepts with the uniform loss function, and it is demonstrated that distribution-free robust learning within a radius of 'r < 1/3' is theoretically equivalent to lossless coding within a reduced radius of 'r' = '(1 - r)/2'.

This study examines how initial conditions of jet and isolated photon producing partons are influenced by their interactions. Specifically, we investigate the six-particle phase space in jet-isolated photon pairs with a fixed rapidity, focusing on cases where a jet and an isolated photon are generated through qg->gamma+j process. In these scenarios, the qg initial state is accompanied by an additional gluon emission, resulting in a highly asymmetric distribution of the six-particle phase space. Notably, the emissions tend to occur off the highly virtual virtuality of the initial state gluon. Utilizing quantum correlation, we are able to access these emissions and redirect them onto the jet and isolated photon initial state partons, effectively equalizing their virtualities. In this study, we utilize short distance positions of the six emitted partons to construct bootstrap initial conditions, which are valid for both NLO calculations and valid for a wide range of infrared-safe observables and valid for a wide range of scale variations and valid for a wide range of virtualities and valid for a wide range of scale variations.

Using the colored multiple zeta values (CMZV) evaluation developed by Borden and Tsumura, we analyze Im(ℓ(2)) and related values, including alternating variations. We demonstrate that the evaluation of alternating versions requires a wider range of CMZV levels than the non-altering version. This finding is achieved through a novel approach involving the reflection of CMZV via the gamma function, generalizing Bortz's work on the reflection of l-level CMZV.

A comprehensive examination has been conducted onWISE 1548-3132, identifying it as a subdwarf with extremely low metallicity and utilizing multi-wavelength data to accurately measure its distance and velocity in space. The analysis involved optical spectroscopy to determine fundamental properties such as temperature, mass, radius, and chemical composition, which revealed a effective temperature of 2450 K, along with deformed gravity fields and an oblate shape with magnitude |Ob-1| = 10^-6 to 10^-5. The presence of water vapor in the atmosphere was detected through Ks band spectroscopy, but strange absorption patterns at H and Ks band peaks suggest the presence of unknown compounds in the atmosphere. The object's albedo is highly reflective, at a minimum of 0.4 in the Ks band, and its obliquity is thought to be large and possibly near 90 degrees, influenced by the presence of the WSE-CH1 companion. The existence of the warmer, L-subdwarf companion, companion WSE-CH1, was also confirmed.

Our research on high-energy nuclear collisions reveals an intriguing particle production pattern. In a collision involving two protons, the ratio of certain particles like particles and particles peaks at a specific momentum level, around one GeV per particle. As the collision involves more particles, the peak of this ratio occurs at lower momentum levels. As the collision involves more particles, the ratios of particles to particles at high momentum levels become more pronounced. This is exemplified by the fact that the particles to particles ratio peaks at around eight MeV per particle.

Process calculations involving parton-parton scattering at the second order of perturbative QCD require knowledge of double parton distribution functions (DPDs), which differ from standard distribution functions as the former accounts for the simultaneous distribution of two parton flavors within a hadron. However, the application of DPDs is limited by current measurement capabilities, which make it impossible to directly constrain them experimentally. Therefore, theoretical predictions are essential for exploring the potential of the LHC and the future HL-LHC to constrain DPDs through the calculation of second-order processes. With upcoming facilities such as the Electron-Ion Collider, HELICollider, and high-energy colliders, direct constraints on DPDs become feasible, expanding their potential applications to the description of nuclear modifications and evolution in p-A and A-A collisions, as well non-perturbative aspects of parton spacetime evolution.

This study reviews up-to-date information about the chemical and physical properties of Martian and Lunar soil, and examines the feasibility of using them for additively manufactured concrete and in-situ metal production through powder processing. A key finding is that the difference in oxygen content between Martian and Lunar soil plays a significant role in determining the potential applications of each material. Martian soil's low iron oxide levels make it a promising feedstock for cement production, while the high oxygen content in Lunar material expands its application beyond concrete production to in-situ metal production. In contrast, the lack of oxygen in Martian soil limits in-situ metal production, but the abundance of iron makes it a suitable feedstock for cement and concrete. Both materials can also be used as concrete additives to improve their properties. Moreover, Lunar oxygen-rich soil can be used as a feedstock for in-situ cement and metal production, while the abundance of iron makes it a suitable feedstock for in-situ metal production.

The behavior of a thin liquid film flowing over a fibrous surface under the influence of gravity has been analyzed using the Stokes equations, under the condition that the surface tension is consistent across the liquid-olid interface. By reducing the problem using the Reynolds number, we examined how slip occurring at specific points on the surface influences drop formation, leading to an unstable film that produces irregular patterns of liquid pools separated by flowing connections, and we explored how these patterns emerge based on the distribution of slip conditions along the surface and their spatial distribution.

The Prospector framework is used for determining star formation rates (SFRs) and understanding stellar populations in galaxies through a Bayesian approach. As no objective standards exist for comparison, our goal is to leverage a unique opportunity to validate Prospector-derived SFRs using $\hbox{H}\alpha$ emission line width ( $v_{\rm{line}}$) and recent research connecting $\hbox{H}\alpha$ luminosity to SFRs when $v_{\rm{ionization capacity}}$ is held constant. This study employs the Prospector model to analyze data from 11 galaxies with high-quality spectroscopy from the SDSS. By finding $v_{\rm{line}}$ and optical color measurements for each galaxy and conducting Bayesian inference with the help of PyMultinest, we use the prior information on stellar populations to narrow down our solution space. By fitting a linear regression model to the relationship between $\hbox{H}\alpha$ luminosity and $v_{\rm{line}}$, we establish a more generalizable connection. Ultimately, our research provides a valuable tool for evaluating SFRs in a broader context beyond local galaxies.

Consider the connection between quadratic categories and certain braided auto-equivalences of nilpotent categories of order two, which we call the exceptional structure. Recent research found that simple tensor categories equivalent to nilpotent categories of order two exhibit this exceptional structure. Building on this, we now show that the same applies to simple tensor categories over a field of order two. Furthermore, we discovered that the category of representations of a Skew Group type and the nilpotent category of order two are linked through this exceptional structure. Interestingly, the properties of Skew Group type can be fully described by the properties of quadratic forms on a free abelian group of rank two, allowing the representation categories to be classified accordingly.

We examine the Fisher-KPP equation in a generic n-dimensional space for n greater than 1, given by the partial differential equation $\partial_t u = \Delta u + u(1-u)$ with initial condition $0 \leq u_0 \leq 1$. Although 57-year-old by-now classical theory is generally known, we provide a novel, straightforward, and well-documented approach that young PDE practitioners can easily grasp. By doing so, our method significantly simplifies the understanding of the equation's regularity properties, asymptotic behavior, front speed, and profile.

This paper details our group's approach for tackling the UbiComp 2021 Challenge in the UbiData category, which involves classifying written actions through temporal data generated by a wearable accelerometer and gyroscope placed on users' wrists. Our unique method capitalizes on the ubiquitous nature of smartphones,人对手机的自然握持姿态, which provides an extra layer of information for accurately interpreting this specific activity. Initially, we employ a neural network to extract relevant features from the time-series data, and then apply a support vector machine to perform the classification task, achieving superior results when utilizing smartphone-related information.

The paper presents a probabilistic approach to duration modeling, distinct from traditional methods that model the mean or variance in isolation. By starting with an unspecified prior for a duration, the approach utilizes regression-based techniques to analyze its components, specifically modeling the distribution of residual variances through a log-normal approximation of scaled residuals' geometry log-values, while merging systematic residuals via the Power Transformation method. Consequently, the posterior distribution for the duration, log p(D|𝒵), is derived as normal, characterized by a variance that integrates both modeled and unmodeled components of the original distribution, effectively capturing skewness in the duration distribution. A novel geometry log-moment measure difference metric is introduced to quantitatively compare the post and pre-model fit quality, providing a comprehensive metric to assess model fit and enable conservative model selection through information theoretic criteria. Furthermore, the approach is enhanced by introducing a Paired Task Simulation to generate diverse data samples and facilitating model comparison and validation.

Long-term monitoring of species populations at a given location is crucial. Standard occupancy models, although producing reliable results, can be computationally intensive due to their reliance on numerical methods like Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulations. However, by leveraging the advantages of Bayesian modeling, it is possible to enhance computational efficiency and develop novel, innovative approaches. This paper outlines four distinct Bayesian strategies to further streamline occupancy modeling. Additionally, it introduces the case for adopting a hierarchical model framework for combined estimation of multiple occupancies across various sites.

This paper introduces the Skincare project, a collaborative venture between engineers, doctors, and computer scientists to create innovative intelligent diagnostic and predictive tools for skin disease. The project's objective is to support general practitioners, dermatologists, and patients in providing high-quality, cost-effective, and accessible skin healthcare. A crucial element involves embedding the project tools within clinical and patients' ecosystems to provide insight and support at each stage of the patient journey. In the short term, a system for non-urgent dermato-radiological imaging analysis has been developed to support the analysis of clinical-acquisition images of the skin and related radiological junctions. By embedding this tool into real-world settings, the accuracy and performance of it has been enhanced and evaluated through evaluation with the involvement of general practitioners and dermatologists. Additionally, plans and insights regarding the long-term deployment of it are discussed along with the potential impact of it on healthcare systems.

Employing Type Ia supernovae to determine the acceleration of the universe necessitates accounting for systematic uncertainties and the natural variability of these events. While conventional models use a minimum $\chi^2$ fit to six physical properties, often assuming unconnected errors and uniform prior distributions, our study proposes an enhanced training method for supernovae. By introducing a correlation penalty into the learning process, our model effectively captures covariant mistakes and the interdependence of variability in supernovae minima. Using five publicly available datasets, we demonstrate that our method yields narrower constraints on cosmological parameters without the need for manual data adjustment. Furthermore, we show that a correlated penalty train significantly enhances the usefulness of low-quality data by reducing their reliance on precise data and diminishes the need for data resampling, thereby facilitating more efficient use of forthcoming supernovae datasets for precise cosmological measurements.

Observations of the galaxy NGC 4436, an edge-on spiral with a large bar, were conducted using the Mopra Radio Telescope to study its CO gas distribution and kinematics. The observations, conducted at 11 frequencies, covered a 30 kpc area. Significant co-extended CO gas was found in the galaxy's disk, with a minimum of 2.1 solar masses per year leaving the galaxy at its edges. The gas within the galaxy is rotating in a specific plane, and its velocity field, when combined with prior knowledge of the galaxy's structure, was used to map out the CO gas distribution. The total CO gas mass in the galaxy was found to be at least 3.4 times 10 to the 7 power solar masses. The CO gas within the galaxy shows a distinct break in its velocity pattern, and its distribution appears to be influenced by the galaxy's external forces. The CO gas distribution within the galaxy is not as extensive as its molecular gas distribution in other galaxies, and its morphology is affected by the galaxy's interactions and environment. The CO gas distribution within the galaxy is also linked to the galaxy's star formation, where the CO gas is least present in areas of high star formation. The CO gas within the galaxy is not as extensive as the neutral gas, where the mass outflow rate of neutral gas was found to be 2.5 times the star formation rate.

The interaction of spherical particles with fluid plumes was investigated through numerical simulations, examining the influence of particles on plume radius and fluid velocity. Realized by imposing an initial disturbance within a particle-laden plume of power-law fluid, the simulations revealed distinct behaviors under varying flow conditions. When the plume's intrinsic buoyancy acted in the same direction as the particles', minimal effects were observed, whereas a reverse direction led to notable enhancements in entrainment. Further analysis indicated that particle clustering at the plume's leading and trailing edges drove this enhanced entrainment, a phenomenon absent in the absence of particles. Contrasting our results with the theoretical predictions of book model, the validation of this model's applicability within a confined range of particle Froude numbers was confirmed, with the theoretical model's reliance on particle-laden shear instability to explain the enhanced entrainment confirmed.

In general graph-based models of contagion where vertices represent individuals and edges represent interactions, it's generally observed that the rate at which the contagion spreads is directly related to the power of the average degree, denoted as <k>. However, this same relationship is observed to be inconsistent in models where the underlying structure is a hypergraph. Using numerical simulations to solve the mean-field differential equations governing the system, it's discovered that in random hypergraphs, the degree-based distribution of the infection rate does not uniformity conform. The rarest occurrences of high-degree individuals do not significantly contribute to the most prevalent types of infection events. The conclusion is that in random hypergraphs, the most frequent infection events are characterized by small-sized interaction groups, a finding that is supported by the theoretical prediction that the critical exponent for infection rate variations is approximately equal to -1.05. The underlying mechanism of this phenomenon is that the randomness of the hypergraph's structure mitigates the impact of the individual connections.

Investigating the interaction between magnetic and vibrational modes in ferromagnetic nickel and antiferromagnetic chromium bilayers reveals unexpected findings. Under the application of compressive strain at 1.5%, a previously unobserved radial spin configuration emerges. By employing spin-resolved resonant inelastic x-ray scattering, we verify that this unusual texture arises due to the strain-induced modification of magnetism and phonon-magnon coupling. Notably, the in-plane Raman-active phonons demonstrate significant application of resonant magnetic coupling to a low-energy antiferromagnetic mode that exhibits a considerable increase in magnetic interaction strength. The observed increase suggests that strain can be a powerful tool for controlling magnetic properties through mechanical means, opening up novel avenues for the design of highly efficient nanomechanical devices that leverage spin-resonant phenomena.

Our previous models of magnetic activity in medium-mass stars exhibited a diverse and intricate behavior characterized by three primary patterns. To further analyze the underlying mechanisms responsible for these patterns, we conducted an analytical study and explored the occurrence of magnetic cycles in slowly rotating stars. We discovered and analyzed three distinct types of magnetic cycles and found that kinematic dynamos can produce these cycles in slowly rotating stars, in contrast to our asymptotic models, which typically yield asymptotic non-cyclic behavior in such stars. We quantified the occurrence of these cycles in terms of the duration and frequency of their occurrence, and found that the occurrence of each magnetic cycle is influenced by different regions in the parameter space. We also found that magnetic and non-magnetic activity can coexist in some regions, and that the occurrence of magnetic cycles can be controlled by the convective turnover time and the ratio of the pressure scale height to the stellar radius.

Deep learning models have demonstrated exceptional performance in handling multiple outputs or inputs with multiple outputs. By leveraging the connection between data points, these models enhance performance while requiring reduced amount of labeled data, which is crucial since each label typically incurs a significant cost to obtain. A recent work utilized structural equations to model the relationship between variables, achieving great results in tasks such as multiple choice questions and transcription. Building upon this, we introduce a method to learn a shared embedding for multiple tasks within a single learning process, allowing the model to discover and utilize latent relationships between tasks that other approaches might overlook. We test our approach on several tasks, including multiple choice questions, machine transcription, and clinical note transcription. The results show that our method outperforms a strong baseline and par on the professional level after fine-tuning, leading to improvements of up to 10% in added-calibration experiments while achieving comparable results in real-world scenarios.

mc-Java is an upgraded version of the well-known Java model checker, created by C. Seidel and et. al., designed for checking multi-threaded program operations. Based on the traditional symbolic model checker model, it incorporates a symbolic execution engine for handling multi-threaded operations, a threading simulation system, and a symbolic execution database for enhancing efficiency in repeated checks, specifically in shared operations. To test mc-Java's (the McMini model checker, inspired by SEAL and based on an ISO/IEEE standard for symbolic execution database adaptation) speed, we compared it to the original implementation, finding it significantly faster in various thread operations, such as checking object clone, list remove, and object equal using Collections.SynchronizedCollection and Collections.concurrentLinkedHashSet. Notably, mc-Java can check these operations up to 8 times faster with 8 threads. With the addition of a thread threading optimization, which manages thread management, we found it significantly faster, up to 20 times faster in some operations.

Recently, WhatsApp has implemented new features to limit the sharing of unknown and potentially harmful information, a move that has led to speculation about the company's intentions to curb the spread of misinformation. Although the company has been working on tackling the misinformation issue, there has been a lack of clear information about the changes made. In an effort to address misinformation, WhatsApp has introduced new mechanisms to limit the forward button's effectiveness and has begun to identify and block unknown information, as well as to display a warning when users forward such content. Our system, MisInfoCab, utilizes intelligent techniques to identify content that is being shared beyond its intended scope, as well as to track the spread of misinformation within social groups. It aims to reverse the negative effects of misinformation by limiting the spread of such content and has been tested through various experiments to evaluate its performance.

Our study examines how genetic mutations influence population diversity over time using a discrete-time model on the space $\ell^2(\mathbb{R})$. A specific rule is used to select parents based on their location in the population. If their combined positions fall within a designated area, their mutation produces a diverse offspring. It is demonstrated that without mutation, convergence to a single population state occurs at an rate of $O(2^{-\frac{1}{2} t})$. Conversely, with mutation frequency $\lambda$, a population state with diverse characteristics can be achieved.

In our research, we introduce an innovative approach for identifying speech artifacts in spoofing countermeasures by leveraging spectral features and an attention mechanism within a convolutional neural network. By combining these elements, the system efficiently captures crucial details from the speech spectrum and pinpointes the most essential features for accurate artifact detection, particularly in regions that contain significant information about the recorded speech. Following this, we develop a multi-faceted evaluation framework for comparing auxiliary metrics across various subsets of speech artifacts generated by different synthesis methods. Using this approach in an independent evaluation with the NIST SPCm 2020 dataset, the proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-systems and demonstrates superior generalisation capabilities across different synthesisers.

This review comprehensively connects supergravity to quantum gravity low-energy theories, as well as low-energy effective theories originating from string theory, highlighting the diverse connections through multidisciplinary approaches. The comparison to weight networks Hoge and Lee, 2013, who effectively linked various theories for magnetic materials and their signatures to experimental data, Hoge et al., 2016, is appreciable. We address three critical questions: (1) the relationship between supergravity and low-energy effective theories derived from string theory, specifically F-theory compactifications; (2) the connection to quantum gravity low-energy theories, focusing on the bottom-up approach; and (3) the underlying reasons for the success of Supergravity in describing the universe, considering its potential standard model limitations. Our analysis, particularly regarding Kachru, Kallosh, Linde, and Muligan's KKLMMT model, who incorporated the best features of string theory's landscape, ultimately demonstrates that Supergravity's success stems from its successful integration of the eight N=8 supergravity multiplets with the four graviton multiplets, achieving a seamless unification with General Relativity, while highlighting the need to explore the full "string theory landscape," exploring diverse string vacuum states, as an essential aspect of understanding the universe's fundamental forces and properties.

The spatial and temporal coherence of photons generated using a non-resonant pump in a silicon microdisk is examined by utilizing both a fundamental pump mode and higher-order modes, and is explored through the implementation of interferometers, spectral filters, and the measurement of single-photon and photon pair patterns. The study also investigates the influence of the pump propagation direction on the coherence functions of photon pairs and the observation of temporal anti-correlation and anti-bunching of photon pairs. Furthermore, the study analyzes the origin of non-reciprocal coherence based on the mode symmetry and the overlap of photon pair and pump modes.

Investigating electronic properties of silicon surface oxide formed through electrochemical etching, which is crucial to understanding silicon's behavior at interfaces with liquids, has been conducted using Hall effect measurements. By examining samples of silicon surface oxide formed via anodization in different concentrations of sodium chloride solutions, researchers found that the carrier concentration in etched silicon was $10^{15}$ cm$^{-2}$, significantly lower than that of buffer oxide etched silicon at $10^{13}$ cm$^{-2}$. Furthermore, by altering the potential difference, which influences the thickness of the silicon surface oxide, researchers observed that the carrier concentration could be manipulated. Notably, by conducting measurements at various temperatures, researchers discovered that the etched region of silicon was not intrinsically doped.

A key decision-point arises in the proof that the real line cannot be divided into equinumerous closed sets with equal powers of the continuum, specifically whether to apply the Axiom of Choice or Selection principles (specifically $AC_{<\omega}$) to ensure equivalent cardinality for sets of appropriate size. However, an alternative approach exists, illustrated through an example of partitioning the real line into Borel sets of different cardinalities, without relying on the Axiom of Choice. Consequently, the specific instance of $AC_{<\omega}$ is irreducible, as demonstrated by another scenario involving partitioning a set into two infinite sets of the same power, which cannot be achieved through a specific principle ($\mathbb{N}\text{-AC}_{<\omega}$).

This paper delves into the concept of short-term reversal trading and its interconnectedness with commodity trading. By employing this strategy, traders can consistently earn a modest daily profit, albeit at a lower annual rate due to the nature of reversal trading's weekly profitability nature. notably, the strategy requires no upfront investment, allowing a substantial portion of the generated income to be reinvested, thereby increasing traders' wealth in tandem with their generated income. an intriguing aspect of this study is the examination of whether commodity trading can serve as a mutually beneficial endeavor for both the trader and their investors, with the analysis focusing largely on the ethical implications surrounding this premise.

A significant issue arises in the area of dynamic protocol detection, which is employed by network monitoring tools and invasive testing tools like Wireshark and Tetris in evading malicious activities. The current methods for evasion are difficult to implement and have limited implications. This study identifies flaws in the dynamic protocol detection mechanism and develops two categories of hyper-automated attack vectors for evading such activities. The first category, which involves traffic emulation attacks, focuses on attacking a single protocol, while the second category, which involves traffic synthesis attacks, combines multiple protocols to attack simultaneously. The effectiveness of these hyper-automated vector categories has been demonstrated through the second category's successful evasion of Wireshark and similar tools, with up to a 97% improvement in accuracy compared to standard traffic emulation attacks.

When interacting with magnetic films, superconducting strips and wedges significantly alter the spread of magnons, particularly under varying critical current levels. Our theoretical framework for studying magnon propagation also reveals that under specific conditions, magnons can induce a transition from the superconducting to the normal state in proximity to the magnetic film. Notably, this proximity effect is not symmetric, exhibiting distinct behaviors based on whether magnons flow towards or away from the interface. These findings have potential implications for designing efficient spin transport devices that leverage both magnons and superconducting electrons as carriers.

Current approaches in zero-shot federated learning predominantly rely on transferring L2 regularisation parameters from a pre-trained server. However, these methods face limitations due to their inability to account for diverse data sets and models not seen during the regularisation pre-training. A new framework for zero-shot federated learning has been developed to overcome this challenge. By utilizing the T-regularised entropy constraint on each client and using the 1/Tth quantile of loss distribution as the regularisation parameter, it is ensured that the regularisation parameter is dynamically adjusted on each client. Extensive evaluations using ImageNet and TaskNet datasets demonstrate the superiority of this proposed framework over existing methods, including Edgy and RegNet.

A crucial transformation in quantum information processing on high-dimensional systems involving multiple photons is the quantum Fourier transform (QFT). We have developed a method to perform a controlled version of the QFT on D-dimensional systems using circuits composed of linear optical elements. The proposed approach minimizes the use of non-linear processes by leveraging pure linear optical methods. Furthermore, we have explored its potential application in implementing quantum oracles in algorithms based on the Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm.

In a hybrid passive system consisting of an access point and an intelligent surface, accurate channel modeling is crucial, yet the increased complexity of such networks leads to significant channel degradation. We address a variously-structured channelestimation problem, incorporating the intelligent surface, where an optimization-based method jointly-calculates all relevant channel components, providing an closed-form solution, proven to converge to the optimal result under specific conditions. We also examine the influence of the number of surface units, the size of the data set, and the level of channel instability on the resulting estimation, along with comparisons to existing techniques in the literature. The proposed optimization-based approach delivers superior performance, especially when the number of system units is modest, and is sensitive to channel instability, while also delivering better results than existing techniques across various scenarios.

In a study examining the content of online news reports about COVID-19 across Spain and its regions, researchers analyzed data from 146 news outlets using a large-scale text mining approach. They collected over 20 million report texts between March 2020 and January 2021. The findings were cross-validated with survey responses from over 11,000 Spaniards. It was discovered that local news coverage varied significantly based on area population size, with greater emphasis given by larger populations. Notable patterns of information dissemination and content were also identified, including specific focus areas among the most covered news topics.

The issue of scaling counting tasks in animals with varying environments is crucial for understanding the basis of counting in humans. While it is known that animals can perform counting tasks within the scope of their training, it is not clear if they can extrapolate their counting skills to larger numbers. Our study investigates whether animals can count beyond their trained limits using the task of discriminating dot pairs of a linearly increasing value. Three bird species were used - New Caledonian crows, common raptors, and flocks of starlings - and were trained in a discrimination task using dot patterns. We found that all bird species were able to count beyond their trained limits by testing them with dot pairs of a linearly increasing value. Our results show that animals can use systematic extrapolation to count beyond their trained limits.

We introduce xor filters, the first probabilistic space-saving filters to have constant time verification speed, user-independent false positive rates, and significantly lower memory usage. Xor filters achieve up to 10x better performance and a 10x decrease in memory usage compared to the most efficient variants of Bloom and Bloomier filters, while using comparable methods to Bloom filters but applying them to the problem of linear algebra problem.
This article establishes a correspondence between divisorial Zariski decomposition and Alexandrov body construction, dividing it into locally finite and infinitely finite cases.

The level of detail in financial transaction data can offer valuable insights into market movements, yet the long-term nature of these insights presents an issue when using them for short-term trading. Historical transaction data has been utilized to determine the time frame over which meaningful market information is accumulated. A novel method was developed to compare retention times across different periods, time series, and levels of detail in financial transaction data, taking into account the specific characteristics of each record, such as frequency and volume. When examining Nasdaq data spanning one year across five different time frame intervals (from 10 ms to 6 min), the study discovered that the retention periods vary significantly, from around 30 for the 10 ms interval to around 3000 for the 6 min interval. Furthermore, the study found that incorporating a 6 min average would result in information loss for traders aiming to profit over shorter time frames of 10 ms to 10 min.

FLVoogd, a clustering framework, processes personal data in an encrypted format using a modified fully homomorphic encryption technique. 
The system produces cluster centers and assigns data points without revealing a participant's data, and without a participant's private information.
FLVoogd incorporates LSH-based co-clustering to efficiently handle large datasets by leveraging two approaches, one of which is the approximate calculation of Hamming distances using batch operations on polynomial rings.
Through our implementation, we prove that each component of FLVoogd provides security against neutral and malicious threats.
The authors compare the performance efficiency of a combination of MLPG, FL-MP2K, and FLVoogd, using real-world data from the UCI repository.
Results show that although each step of FLVoogd is less efficient than its classical counterparts, it offers improved performance compared to its classical version by as much as 3.5 times faster.
Despite producing the same clustering results, FLVoogd is not as effective as the classical system due to noise accumulation during processing.
However, we have designed a method to reduce noise at the start of the process without compromising the system's security.

The autonomous vehicle challenge 2020 entry utilizes simulated data for pre-training, leveraging a multi-GPU approach with a single-gpu setup for evaluation due to resource constraints. A novel architecture is proposed, featuring an encoder-decoder framework for various tasks and the use of task-agnostic pre-training with task-specific fine-tuning. Since the entry relies on pre-trained weights, it exhibits a significant sim2real performance gap, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed architecture in improving this sim2real discrepancy.

The increasing realism of deepfake media poses significant concerns, including widespread misinformation dissemination in upcoming elections. Although deepfake tools can manipulate media, they can also provide a means of inverting and recovering original content from altered videos and images. Although their potential exists, a possible connection between deepfake manipulation and information verification has not been thoroughly explored in current research due to the limited capabilities of inversion techniques and the vast amount of required training data. This study aims to overcome these challenges, and for the first time, we evaluate whether machine learning models can accurately classify deepfake manipulation models based on large public datasets, even though these datasets are significantly smaller than those typically used in deepfake inversion research. Our initial findings suggest a strong potential for classifying inversion methods and identifying generated images with high accuracy, and our framework is designed for efficient generalization to unrelated datasets, even those with unrelated styles and concepts. Our proposed framework, DeepRadar, utilizes a shared data-independent backbone to achieve this classification task. Through extensive experiments on multiple datasets, we demonstrate improved performance across various inversion methods and configurations, and the results of our research are presented in this paper.

We use a specialized model to examine the potential atmospheres of terrestrial planets located around nearby stars in the UV-optical spectrum. Our simulations indicate that two distinct atmospheric compositions are possible: (1) a more substantial atmosphere, weighing 0.1-10 kg/m^2, and likely retains carbon and nitrogen gases, or original volcanic gases, and (2) a thinner atmosphere, weighing 0.01-0.1 kg/m^2, where UV photolysis strips away heavy molecules, leaving behind light gases. For both scenarios, our predictions align with data from the James Webb Space Telescope, and we find that a massive atmosphere could display signs of liquid water and methane, while a thin atmosphere might display a signature similar to a CO2 atmosphere. Our analysis confirms that M-dwarfs can indeed support the development of terrestrial atmospheres.

The classic Hopfield network excels at association and retrieval, yet its learning is limited to random bit patterns due to Hebbian learning's simplicity. A proposed MCP network bridges the gap between Hopfield and McCulloch-Pitts architectures, offering an enhanced version of Hopfield that is more adaptable while maintaining association and pattern learning capabilities. By employing a modified sign function, MCP now represents a fully connected system. Analysis revealed that MCP can efficiently learn multiple patterns, including permutations of the input, and with only a 5% error rate. Simulation results indicate an optimal block length of about 70 and a capacity of approximately 14 stored blocks, outperforming the permutation-limitation-free Hopfield which stops at a capacity of 16.

This paper introduces OutOVi, a state-of-the-art scene text recognition model that outperforms existing approaches, including Acknowledge was recognized for its contributions in this field. OutOVi builds on the successful architecture of OCR-30K and incorporates an innovative dataset, the OOV dataset, comprising 470,000 real-world outdoor signs with diverse content and styles. We also introduce a new sign collection method to bolster OOV dataset's variety, as well as a simplified and efficient training strategy for recognition models. Through comprehensive evaluations, OutOVi demonstrates exceptional performance on AID, OT_Roblo, TotalText, and OOV itself, achieving an impressive 86.76% accuracy on OOV, a challenging large-scale dataset. We attribute OutOVi's impressive success to the integration of the OOV dataset and a streamlined training technique.

The computation of isolated system solutions in the form of solution branches is feasible with accurate bounds on all variables and parameters through verified numerics. This method can be extended to compute entire branches of solutions for systems that depend on parameters, and has been successfully applied to stabilize metal strip production processes with precise parameters and solutions. We demonstrate how to stabilize these processes using a novel method and outline the steps to guide the branch continuation, validating a practical application using open-source software.

Industrial statistical changes in process monitoring can be analyzed by dividing data into distinct time-based segments, yet current techniques often struggle with the high computational demands and sensitivity to changes associated with large datasets. To address this, a new method is presented, leveraging reduced-dimensional projections to efficiently detect changes and identify specific failures within processes. Furthermore, it is possible to optimize the performance of change point detection and failure mode isolation simultaneously by considering the trade-off between computational complexity and performance in a concave optimization framework. The outcome is a set of optimized subspaces that enhance identification accuracy while reducing computational requirements, thus potentially enabling real-time implementation. To support this, a method is provided to determine the optimal number of subspaces based on available data, along with approaches for handling unknown failure types and scenarios. Ultimately, the approach is validated on two case studies, demonstrating significant improvements in performance and computational efficiency.

Previous examination of the Gaia-Sausage Enceladus (GSE) dwarf galaxy's formation suggested a brief merger event. Yet, this conclusion may have been biased by concerns about the GSE structure. This study investigated the timing and duration of another GSE's companion dwarf galaxy, Wukong (WUK), using deep photometric data from the Gaia and Pan-STACCS surveys. The researchers identified distinct GSE and WUK star clusters and found their formation and dissolution patterns to be distinct. The Cluster Dwarf Galaxy's formation ended some time ago, but GSE's formation spanned several hundred million years. The study's findings indicate that using photometric data Wildy et al.'s analysis can accurately determine a galaxy's formation time frame and highlight variations in the GSE's formation process.

For a perfect group $G$ with $||G||_k$ defining the regular representation of $G$ in the $k$-th stage of the Postnikov tower of $\mathbb{Z}$, we establish an equivalence between the homotopy orbit spectrum $(\mathbb{Z}[[G]])_{hG}$ and $\mathbb{Z}$ provided that the order of the outer automorphism group of $G$ is relatively prime to the $k$-th stage's order of $G$. Furthermore, we define an invariant for perfect groups that reflects this equivalence, specifically the maximal $k$ within its invariant set, we demonstrate its locality property, establish a bound for its value when $G$ is a finite simple group, and determine its value for abelian groups.

Acquiring labeled data can be expensive and time-consuming, however, labeling strategies that focus most informative cases can accelerate the acquisition process. Active learning aids in identifying these crucial instances through active case selection, while selective labeling aids in process optimization. The combination of active learning and selective labeling can be challenging, as they tackle distinct problems, whereas their integration presents new opportunities to tackle them jointly. Our research focuses on combining these concepts, as they can be beneficial when integrating both active learning and selective labeling, especially when aiming to label partially, due to varying costs and constraints. We developed a novel framework that combines these concepts, as adapted from active learning and selective labeling, as their individual formulations. This new framework, selective active learning, enables their joint optimization, however, it poses complex challenges. We introduce a new method that addresses this introduced complexity, as it can be applied to any base active learning method, while also retains theoretical guarantees. Our experimental findings demonstrate the effectiveness of this new method, as it outperforms its individual components and existing methods that combine them.

A even-numbered layers of EuS on an InAs substrate was grown using a specific technique in order to examine its electronic properties through various methods. The results from temperature-dependent measurements using techniques such as scanning tunneling microscopy and low energy electron diffraction indicated the presence of arsenic vacancies at the interface that interact with 4f states of europium, exhibiting heavy magnetic behavior influenced by temperature. The temperature dependence of this interaction was analyzed using a model, providing insight into its underlying mechanisms. The findings suggest that magnetic states originating from valence band energy levels can significantly contribute to the electronic band structure, potentially benefiting the development of magnetic topological insulator heterostructures by modifying their band structures through engineering arsenic vacancies.

This paper establishes a connection between three entities: a determinacy principle in a specific context (Borel Wadge determinacy), a complex version of a mathematical theory (second-order arithmetic with a specific axiom about infinite sequences), and a property in an equivalent formulation of that theory. Specifically, we prove that Borel Wadge determinacy is equivalent to a combination of two principles in this reformulated theory: a basic property and a statement regarding countable sequences in a mathematical framework.

Neural network models have become increasingly complex, leading to demands for more efficient processing. While previous studies introduced methods like ClickTrain and SortTrain for reducing model sizes through pruning, our research delves into the internal structure of attention models and develops a more aggressive and efficient approach. Unlike traditional methods, our technique captures the flow of internal data and discards redundant operations based on input-output relationships, enabling better performance than previous methods without incurring significant accuracy losses. We validate our findings by applying ClickTrain to various models, including the BERT and BART architectures, and demonstrate its effectiveness in our real-world tasks of searching and generating answers.

This study introduces a substructural modal logic by extending the semantics of relevance logic with relations that are external to the logic itself. Our findings show that certain modal logics underlying non-spacelike order in special relativity can be accurately modeled through this framework. Specifically, utilizing the graph representing a given Minkowski spacetime as the logic's external semantics enables fully first-order characterizations of various subsets of the corresponding modal logic. Moreover, our characterization encompasses the distinction between causal connectability and actual occurrence, thereby providing a precise logical expression of the concept of time travel.

The initial period of neutron star coalescence produces intense simultaneous emissions of gravitational and electromagnetic radiation, a phenomenon that the upcoming generation of Earth-based telescures may be able to observe, a phenomenon that the next generation of Earth-based telescures may observe.
Observing these emissions together would provide a wealth of information, including the ability to pinpoint the exact location of the event and identify the mass of the neutron star, which would then facilitate further astronomical observations across various wavelengths.

TOI-5542, a G-type dwarf with 6.8 times the Sun in mass, hosts at least one highly massive planet called TOI-5542b, which has a unique flagship status due to its edgy location in the gap between stars and its significant potential for the exploration of planetary formation and composition through future observations with the James Webb Space Telescope and other space facilities. The space based observations were conducted via the TESS and ground-based data from the Magellan and Keck observatories were carried out through radial velocity measurements. The analysis of the data revealed the extremely heavy planet mass of 11.83 times the mass of the Sun and a semi-major axis of about 2.7 times the radius of the Sun and a semi-major axis of about 2.71 AU. The orbit of the planet is completely circular and a minimum mass of about 11.83 times the mass of the Sun and a semi-major axis of about 2.71 AU. The planet's dense core is about 11.83 times the mass of the Sun and a semi-major axis of about 2.71 AU.
